Re: Member Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial
Member Name: Harper Grant
Member ID: W740585624
Reference Number: POC-BA397EFDB1-13824
Requested Service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT Code 28296
Surgeon: Reyes, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-23
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-19

Dear Member Appeals Department,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for my scheduled hallux valgus correction (bunion surgery), CPT code 28296, to be performed by Dr. Reyes. The denial letter dated August 23, 2026, states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. 

This request is governed by the "Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery" (Doc ID: MSK06-1125.1, Effective Date: 11/15/2025). Under these guidelines, "Hallux valgus surgery is considered medically necessary when ALL the following requirements are met:"

Below, I demonstrate how my medical records satisfy each of these clinical requirements:

1. Skeletal Maturity:
[Insert confirmation of skeletal maturity, e.g., Patient is an adult who is skeletally mature]

2. Clinical Symptoms, Functional Limitation, and Conservative Management:
The guideline requires: "Significant pain and functional limitation of the first metatarsophalangeal joint and/or presence of a pre-ulcer (e.g., Wagner grade 0-1) that persists after at least 12 weeks of supervised conservative management OR nonhealing ulcer at the site of the bunion or the second toe"
* Pain and Function: I have suffered from 14 months of progressive, severe foot pain that is unrelieved by rest. Physical exam reveals a range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side. Functionally, I can no longer tolerate closed shoes, and my clinical records note a significant "ulceration risk over the prominence" of my first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint, representing a pre-ulcer risk.
* Conservative Management: My conservative treatments have spanned over 8 months, far exceeding the 12-week clinical timeline. I have tried and failed oral NSAIDs for 8 months. I also received a corticosteroid injection on June 12, 2026, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. Additionally, I completed an intensive, 8-week course of supervised physical therapy from May 23, 2026, to July 18, 2026 (consisting of 24 completed visits), during which I utilized custom orthotics, activity modification, and wide toe-box footwear. Given that my severe pain and functional limitations persist despite 8 months of comprehensive conservative therapies and 8 weeks of intensive supervised physical therapy, the clinical intent of the 12-week conservative management guideline has been fully met, and immediate surgical correction is required to prevent skin breakdown (ulceration).

3. Radiographic Confirmation:
The guideline requires: "Radiographic confirmation of an elevated hallux valgus angle (HVA), (metatarsophalangeal angle greater than 15 degrees), or intermetatarsal angle (greater than 9 degrees)"
* My weight-bearing foot radiographs from June 27, 2026, confirm a severe structural deformity with a hallux valgus angle (HVA) of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle (IMA) of 17 degrees. Both measurements far exceed the plan's criteria of "greater than 15 degrees" and "greater than 9 degrees", respectively.

4. Vascular Perfusion:
The guideline requires: "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)"
* [Insert physical exam documentation of vascular perfusion, e.g., physical examination by Dr. Reyes confirmed adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion with strong, palpable pedal pulses]

Finally, I do not have any contraindications to surgery; I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, am a non-smoker, and have a BMI of 29. 

Based on my clinical records, I meet all medical necessity criteria outlined in your governing policy. I request that you overturn this denial and authorize CPT code 28296 so that I may proceed with this medically necessary surgery. Please contact Dr. Reyes's office at [Insert Surgeon's Phone Number] if you require any additional medical records.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Harper Grant
